prerequisites: Differentiation and integration of functions in one and more variables.

learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with a basic knowledge of the main concepts and results of probability theory and statistics.
Develop the ability to construct, use, and interpret simple probabilistic and statistical models.

syllabus_topics: Graphical and numerical summaries of data
Measures of location and dispersion, and correlation
Sample spaces and the axioms of probability
Random variables: distributions, mean, and variance
Discrete models: uniform, Bernoulli, binomial, Poisson, and geometric distributions
Continuous models: uniform, normal, and exponential distributions
Joint and conditional distributions, covariance, and independence
Limit theorems: the weak law of large numbers and the central limit theorem
Statistical inference: point estimation, confidence intervals, and hypothesis tests
teaching_methods: Explanations and worked examples on the board
assessment_rules: The exam consists of two parts: a multiple-choice test and a written test with open-ended questions, both taking place on the same day. Students may take the written test only after passing the multiple-choice test. Grading is based on the ability to apply concepts, justify reasoning, use correct scientific language, choose suitable models/methods, check conditions, and interpret results, with scores ranging from Fail to 30 and Honors.
bibliography: Ross, S. M. (2020). Introduction to Probability and Statistics for Engineers and Scientists (6th ed.). Academic Press.
degree: Laurea in Ingegneria Meccanica (Mechanical Engineering), classe L-9 Classe delle lauree in Ingegneria industriale
